cohort: 5573 mothers and their respective twin pairs born live at 34-42 weeks' gestation in Washington State from 1997-2007, with twin A in vertex presentation
finding: Planned cesarean delivery was associated with improved maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to vaginal or cesarean delivery during labor in nulliparous women carrying twins to term.
mod_finding: The lowest rate of combined poor short-term outcomes occurred in mothers and twin pairs delivered by cesarean without labor (23%) and the highest rates occurred in those with operative vaginal or cesarean during labor (39% and 34%, respectively).
